summary: If this letter does not reach you, please let me know at once. Also, I apolo­ gize for the lousy ribbon, but it will get darker if I just keep writing long enough (I’ve had it for several years and have come to know its quirks). How are you, Susan? I would have written long, long ago but we have been busy having a baby. He is a boy named Christopher, and he frowns all the time as if saying, like Queen Victoria, “We are not amused.” I think he anticipated a more well-to-do family, and certainly some other city than Fullerton. They proba­ bly promised him Bob and Barbara Silverberg and Oakland (somebody told me the other day that the Silverbergs’ house cost $750,000). It has a pool in the liv­ ing room, and I hope they all fall in and drown (I’m kidding; what I really hope is that Bob dies and wills the house, plus Barbara, to me.) See, my ribbon is get­ ting darker. I never lie. We moved to a new apartment, but so what, like also we bought a car and a color TV, all so what. The “what” in contrast to the “so what” is that—well, Susan, I’m not sure. I feel sort of down and I wrote two letters to my agent, but that has an impersonal feel to it, and I thought of writing to Carol Carr and other loves up in the Bay Area, but none of them ever answer. I think they just burn mail addressed to Marin County, or else everyone there is dead or crazy or both.
